title: Lesson 23: Agent Patterns: ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, Reflection, and Tool Loops
description: Lesson 22 built the loop by hand. This lesson gives that loop its names. You learn the four patterns that dominate real agent work: ReAct (reason and act interleaved), plan-and-execute (plan first, then execute), reflection (evaluate and revise), and the tool loop they all run on, plus when each one earns its complexity.

questions.question: What distinguishes ReAct from a plain tool-calling loop?
options: It skips tool calls entirely and answers straight from the model's memory.
It interleaves reasoning with each action and observation.
It plans the entire task once before acting.
It runs several agents in parallel.
questions.explanation: ReAct interleaves a natural-language reasoning trace with each action and observation, so the model reasons before it acts instead of firing tools blindly.

questions.question: Why does plan-and-execute often make fewer large-model calls than a ReAct-style agent?
options: It never calls any tools at all.
It re-plans after every single action it takes.
It splits planning from doing, so steps run on cheaper models.
It evaluates its own output against the original request before it answers.
questions.explanation: Plan-and-execute separates planning from doing, so the large model is called for planning and re-planning while individual steps can run on cheaper models.

questions.question: Which pattern adds an evaluate-and-revise pass so an agent can learn from a failed first attempt?
questions.explanation: Reflection adds an actor, an evaluator, and a self-reflection step that scores a trajectory and feeds verbal feedback into the next attempt.
